map.summary: This area builds and runs retrieval-quality tests for the search service. It loads versioned dataset bundles whose files are checked by hash, prepares an isolated search index for each dataset, runs four search styles over every test question, scores how well the results match human relevance labels, and saves reproducible JSON and readable Markdown reports. A local-only debug endpoint and a SciFact dataset builder support this work.
unknowns: How the saved evaluation records in the database connect at runtime to the dataset bundle loader is not shown.
The internal retrieval, scoring, and settings behavior behind the shared search boundary is only inferred from where it is called.
Whether durable ingestion jobs always run inline here or can also be handled by a separate worker service is not traced.
How evaluation scores or saved runs are surfaced to any user interface or external caller beyond the debug endpoint is not described.

diagrams.title: How a dataset becomes a scored report
diagrams.description: A verified dataset bundle is prepared into its own search index, every test question is searched in four ways, results are scored against human relevance labels, and a repeatable report is written.

diagrams.title: How a debug search request is answered
diagrams.description: A local-only request names a dataset and question, the service checks the dataset is prepared, runs one search style in an isolated scope, and returns ranked results or a clear error status.

diagrams.title: How the SciFact test set is built
diagrams.description: A pinned public archive is downloaded and hash-checked, converted into the shared dataset format, trimmed to a deterministic 30-question, 500-document baseline, and re-loaded to prove it is valid.

F0001.statement: The evaluation subsystem package re-exports dataset contracts and a loader from hybrid_rag_search.evaluation.datasets: CorpusRecord, DatasetManifest, EvaluationDataset, JudgmentRecord, QueryRecord, and load_dataset, defining the public evaluation data contract surface.

F0002.statement: The debug search HTTP endpoint POST /debug/search accepts a DebugSearchRequest with dataset limited to synthetic-workspace, scifact, or scifact-subset, a query string (1-4096 chars), and a SearchMode; it refuses requests when settings.app_env is 'production' with a 404, making it local-only.

F0003.statement: debug_search resolves the dataset via selected_dataset, verifies preparation via verify_prepared, then opens an EvaluationSearch context and returns search results with debug=True; ValueError/OSError map to HTTP 409 and RetrievalError/ProviderError map to HTTP 503 with the error code.

F0004.statement: Evaluation scopes use a fixed tenant UUID (EVALUATION_TENANT = 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000201) and derive the collection id deterministically via uuid5 from the dataset corpus hash and configured pipeline version, so the same corpus and pipeline reuse the same collection.

F0005.statement: evaluation_scope rejects datasets whose corpus contains non-document record types ("Day 15 evaluates document corpora only") and maps each corpus record id to a document id via uuid5(collection, record.id).

F0006.statement: selected_dataset loads a dataset by name from a fixed DATASETS mapping (synthetic-workspace, scifact, scifact-subset paths) and raises ValueError for unknown names.

F0007.statement: evaluation_index_settings renames the OpenSearch read and write aliases to a hybrid-rag-eval-{collection_id} prefix so evaluation index creation stays separate from demo aliases and manual rebuilds.

F0008.statement: ensure_evaluation_index checks via an HTTP HEAD for the physical index and, when absent (404), creates it through OpenSearchIndexManager and points the write then read alias; other non-404 statuses are raised as errors.

F0009.statement: ManualActor and ManualPublisher are stand-in components whose send/send_with_options and publish methods are no-ops, allowing durable ingestion jobs to be executed inline by the preparation CLI while retries stay explicit.

F0010.statement: prepare_corpus validates a nonnegative document_delay, prepares the evaluation index, creates a Tenant and Collection row idempotently (on_conflict_do_nothing), and disposes its database engine in a finally block.

F0011.statement: For each corpus record, prepare_corpus computes a sha256 content digest, saves content to LocalFileStorage under a tenant/document key, and inserts a Document row scoped to tenant and collection; if a document already exists, a differing content_hash or source_metadata triggers a ValueError treating prepared documents as immutable.

F0012.statement: prepare_corpus enqueues a durable ingestion job per document and, when the job is not already succeeded, runs run_configured_job inline through ManualActor and the OpenSearch index, raising ValueError with the job id and result if ingestion does not succeed.

F0013.statement: After ingestion, prepare_corpus calls compact_corpus, which POSTs a forcemerge to the evaluation physical index with max_num_segments=1 and flush=true to settle deleted promotion records before benchmarking.

F0014.statement: verify_prepared fails closed: it queries IngestionJob rows for the scope's documents at the scope pipeline version with status 'succeeded', requires the count to equal the corpus size, and requires each completed job's checkpoint to contain an 'index' receipt with a string generation_id and integer chunk_count.

F0015.statement: verify_prepared then queries the evaluation read alias with an aggregation over document_id and generation_id filtered by tenant, collection, and visibility 'ready', and raises ValueError if the observed generations/chunk counts differ from the job receipts, guarding against stale or rebuilt indexes and returning the total ready document count on success.

F0016.statement: The debug search API relies on EvaluationSearch and SearchMode from hybrid_rag_search.evaluation.search and selected_dataset/verify_prepared from evaluation.corpus; the actual retrieval dispatch and scoring behavior of EvaluationSearch is not visible in these excerpts.

F0017.statement: load_dataset loads and validates an evaluation dataset from a directory containing a manifest plus corpus, queries, and judgments JSONL files, returning an immutable EvaluationDataset without mutating the source.

F0018.statement: DatasetManifest must declare schema_version 'evaluation-dataset-v1', purpose 'evaluation', and exactly one entry each for corpus.jsonl, queries.jsonl, and judgments.jsonl, enforced by require_all_files_once.

F0019.statement: load_dataset verifies a SHA-256 hash of each declared dataset file against the manifest and raises DatasetValidationError on mismatch, making content integrity part of the load contract.

F0020.statement: _read_jsonl parses each line as a JSON object against a Pydantic model, rejecting blank lines and non-object lines with line-numbered DatasetValidationError messages.

F0021.statement: CorpusRecord validation distinguishes document versus chunk records: chunks require a document_id and documents must not have one.

F0022.statement: _unique_ids rejects duplicate corpus and query identifiers before cross-referencing, ensuring ID uniqueness within each collection.

F0023.statement: load_dataset enforces referential integrity: every judgment must reference a known query and known corpus target, and the judgment's declared target_type must match the target record's type.

F0024.statement: load_dataset requires every query to have at least one judgment and at least one positive (relevance_grade > 0) judgment, otherwise raising DatasetValidationError.

F0025.statement: load_dataset computes a corpus_hash from the corpus file bytes and a dataset_hash from a newline-joined digest of schema version, dataset id, dataset version, and per-file hashes, enabling reproducible dataset identity.

F0026.statement: StrictModel forbids extra fields and freezes instances, so all dataset records reject unexpected input and are immutable after construction.

F0027.statement: score_ranking deduplicates the ranking while preserving order, then computes recall@5, recall@10, and recall@50 against the set of positively judged documents.

F0028.statement: score_ranking computes mrr@10 as the reciprocal rank of the first relevant document within the top ten, returning 0.0 if none is found.

F0029.statement: score_ranking computes ndcg@10 using graded relevance (2^grade - 1 discounted by log2(rank+1)) and normalizes by an ideal DCG over the top ten judged grades.

F0030.statement: score_ranking enforces input contracts: it raises ValueError if any grade is not an integer between 0 and 3, or if the judgment set contains no positive grade.

F0031.statement: score_ranking treats unjudged documents as grade zero during nDCG and count them against recall and MRR, so only judged-relevant documents earn credit.

F0032.statement: The dataset loader consumes validated on-disk evaluation records and emits tuples of corpus, query, and judgment models plus hashes, which downstream evaluation code (not shown in these excerpts) uses to drive corpus preparation and scoring.

F0033.statement: runner.py is a CLI (main via argparse subcommands prepare/run/compare/export) that orchestrates retrieval-benchmark execution: 'run' loads a named dataset via selected_dataset, applies benchmark_settings and evaluation_index_settings, verifies prepared corpus chunks, then drives evaluate over all queries and all MODES.

F0034.statement: evaluate iterates each query and each retrieval mode, calls the injected search function, trims chunk fields, computes ranking from result documents, scores via score_ranking against per-query judgments, and records metrics, elapsed_ms, chunk_count, document_count and full search result per mode.

F0035.statement: Judgment loading enforces that each query has unique document-type judgments; duplicate target_id or non-document target_type raises ValueError.

F0036.statement: Per-query and per-mode deltas relative to bm25 metrics are computed (delta_vs_bm25) using bm25 as the reference baseline for every other mode.

F0037.statement: Aggregate metrics are the mean across queries for each mode and metric key, with metric names recall@5, recall@10, recall@50, mrr@10, ndcg@10.

F0038.statement: save_report writes both report.json (jsonable_encoder-serialized, sorted keys) and report.md (markdown_report rendering aggregate table plus per-query BM25 differences) into a created output directory.

F0039.statement: compare_reports refuses comparisons when metadata keys dataset/configuration/pipeline_version/index/models/adapters differ or query sets differ, and otherwise reports maximum absolute per-query and aggregate metric drift, noting latency is descriptive only.

F0040.statement: configuration uses an explicit allowlist of Settings fields (opensearch_bm25_* plus listed limits/timeouts/schema version) plus a fixed rrf_rank_constant of 60, expressly to keep credentials and unrelated settings out of reports.

F0041.statement: run_baseline records reproduction metadata: schema identifier, UTC creation time, git HEAD revision and dirty-worktree flag, dataset id/version/hashes/counts, chunk count, pipeline version, resolved OpenSearch indexes, tenant and collection ids, hardware info, caller-supplied cache_state, query delay, execution note, model names, adapters, allowlisted config, metric rules, and a count of hybrid_rerank results with a fallback reason.

F0042.statement: run_baseline resolves OpenSearch indexes by GETting /_alias/<opensearch_read_alias> through an httpx AsyncClient and raising on HTTP error, and captures git revision via subprocess calls to 'git rev-parse HEAD' and 'git diff HEAD --name-only'.

F0043.statement: The runner wires external systems: OpenSearch (via httpx alias lookup and via EvaluationSearch/benchmark_settings), Cohere embedding and rerank models (recorded as adapters 'cohere'), and the durable corpus preparation boundary (verify_prepared, evaluation_scope, prepare_corpus, DATASETS).

F0044.statement: The export subcommand reloads a previously written report JSON from disk and re-renders it to JSON and markdown via save_report, without re-running anything.

F0045.statement: evaluate supports an optional nonnegative query_delay that sleeps between queries; negative values are rejected with ValueError.

F0046.statement: The 'prepare' subcommand runs prepare_corpus for the selected dataset with settings from get_settings and an optional document delay, i.e. the runner also owns corpus setup (delegated to the evaluation.corpus module).

F0047.statement: main is marked as exercised only through documented CLI commands and the module itself is guarded by if __name__ == '__main__', so the entry point is the command line rather than an imported API.

F0048.statement: The concrete behavior inside EvaluationSearch, score_ranking, benchmark_settings, evaluation_index_settings, verify_prepared, selected_dataset, and prepare_corpus is not defined in this excerpt; their roles are inferred from call sites only.

F0049.statement: The SciFact module is a command-line dataset builder: main() parses a required command (download, validate, subset), optional --output and --source paths, defaults output to the versioned cache directory for download/validate and to the subset v1 directory for subset, then prints a summary line after running.

F0050.statement: download_archive fetches the pinned BEIR SciFact zip from a fixed HTTPS URL with redirects and a 60-second timeout, writes it to a temporary '.partial' file, verifies its SHA-256 against SCIFACT_ARCHIVE_SHA256, and only then atomically replaces the destination, raising ValueError on hash mismatch and removing the partial file in a finally block.

F0051.statement: convert_archive re-verifies the archive hash before reading, extracts 'scifact/qrels/test.tsv', 'scifact/corpus.jsonl' and 'scifact/queries.jsonl' from the zip in memory, maps corpus ids to 'scifact-doc-<id>', query ids to 'scifact-query-<id>', keeps only queries that appear in qrels, converts qrels scores to relevance grades (3 if score>0 else 0), and writes corpus.jsonl, queries.jsonl and judgments.jsonl sorted by id plus a manifest.json recording the source URL, archive hash, license and per-file SHA-256 hashes.

F0052.statement: build_subset selects a deterministic sample from an already-converted dataset: 30 queries by lowest salted SHA-256 of 'scifact-subset-v1:<id>', all their judgments, then fills to exactly 500 documents by the same salted hash ordering, raising ValueError if the source has fewer than 30 queries or 500 documents or if judgments already require more than 500 documents.

F0053.statement: build_subset writes a rewritten manifest labeled dataset_id 'scifact-subset' version 'scifact-subset-v1' that records the parent dataset hash and describes the selection rule, then reloads the output via load_dataset as a final validation before returning the output path.

F0054.statement: The SciFact CLI's validate command performs no explicit branch in main and instead falls through to the shared _summary() call, which loads the target directory with load_dataset and reports dataset id, version, corpus/query/judgment counts and corpus/dataset hashes.

F0055.statement: EvaluationSearch is the single search boundary for evaluation: it holds a Settings copy whose candidate and result limits are pinned to BUDGET=100 via benchmark_settings, and creates the BM25 retriever eagerly while leaving dense, hybrid and reranked retrievers unbuilt until first needed.

F0056.statement: EvaluationSearch.search receives an EvaluationDataset, a query string, a mode in ('bm25','dense','hybrid','hybrid_rerank') and optional metadata filters, raises ValueError on unknown modes, and derives per-dataset index scope and read alias through evaluation_scope and evaluation_index_settings, updating the aliases on the lexical and (if present) dense retrievers.

F0057.statement: Metadata filters accepted by EvaluationSearch.search are restricted to source_type, author, source_date_from and source_date_to; any other key raises ValueError, and source_date_* values are normalized through parse_source_date before being passed as search options alongside tenant_id, collection_id and debug.

F0058.statement: Mode dispatch branches by retriever: bm25 uses the lexical retriever; dense lazily constructs a Cohere embeddings provider and a dense retriever; hybrid adds a HybridRetriever with RRF candidate_limit=BUDGET; hybrid_rerank additionally lazily constructs a Cohere reranker and a RerankedRetriever with settings-derived config. Providers are entered into an AsyncExitStack for the lifetime of the EvaluationSearch context.

F0059.statement: After retrieval, EvaluationSearch.search validates every returned chunk against the prepared evaluation scope, raising ValueError if tenant, collection, document id or pipeline_version mismatch, then annotates each chunk with its rank and mapped evaluation_document_id and produces a de-duplicated document-level ranking keyed by evaluation document id.

F0060.statement: EvaluationSearch.search returns a dict containing mode, a chunks list with document/chunk identity and rank, a documents list of unique ranked document ids, and a trace converted from the selected retriever's trace dataclass via asdict.

F0061.statement: The evaluation subsystem depends on shared retrieval contracts (RetrievalResult, HybridRetriever/RRFConfig, RerankedRetriever, OpenSearch BM25 and dense retrievers) and provider factories configured from Settings, so evaluation runs are wired into the same retrieval stack used elsewhere rather than a separate implementation.

F0062.statement: EvaluationSearch is an async context manager that opens and closes its AsyncExitStack via __aenter__/__aexit__, so lazily created provider resources (embeddings, reranker) are released when the shared search boundary exits.

F0063.statement: Dataset integrity is enforced at multiple points: archive and file-level SHA-256 hashes, a pinned version label, and a full load_dataset re-read between building and returning a dataset, so a corrupted or altered SciFact source is rejected before downstream use.

F0064.statement: The SciFact subset is explicitly described as a pipeline baseline with 30 queries and 500 documents, not the full BEIR SciFact, which bounds what evaluation results derived from it can claim.

F0065.statement: The evaluation subsystem persists its domain state as four tenant-scoped PostgreSQL tables: EvaluationDataset (versioned, hash-addressed dataset metadata), Judgment (per-query relevance labels targeting documents or chunks), EvaluationRun (execution status, seed, metrics and error state), and AuditEvent (namespaced action records attributed to a membership). All rows carry tenant_id and most cross-references use composite (tenant_id, id) foreign keys so tenant isolation is enforced at the database level.

F0066.statement: EvaluationDataset enforces integrity through database constraints: name must be non-blank, version must be positive, corpus_hash must be a 64-character lowercase hex SHA-256 digest, dataset_metadata must be a JSON object, and (tenant_id, name, version) is unique. This makes a dataset a versioned, content-addressed artifact.

F0067.statement: Judgment constrains each label: target_type must be 'document' or 'chunk', target_id and query text/keys must be non-blank, relevance_grade must be between 0 and 3, key_facts must be a JSON array and metadata_filters a JSON object. The unique key (tenant_id, dataset_id, query_key, target_type, target_id) prevents duplicate judgments, and the foreign key to evaluation_datasets cascades on delete.

F0068.statement: EvaluationRun records execution lifecycle: a status drawn from the EvaluationRunStatus enumeration (queued, running, succeeded, failed, cancelled) defaulting to queued, a non-negative seed, JSON object metrics, optional error message and started/finished timestamps, with updated_at refreshed on modification. Its dataset and retrieval_config foreign keys are RESTRICT on delete, so a run cannot exist without both.

F0069.statement: AuditEvent captures who did what to which entity: an actor_membership_id (nullable) referencing memberships (RESTRICT), an action matching a namespaced pattern such as 'namespace.event', an entity_type matching a lowercase identifier pattern, a non-blank entity_id, and a JSON object of details, timestamped on insert. This provides an append-oriented audit trail tied to tenant and membership.

F0070.statement: Dataset loading (load_dataset) is deterministic and re-loadable: loading the synthetic workspace dataset twice yields equal objects, exposing a manifest version, 8 corpus records, 12 queries spanning four categories (exact-match, paraphrase, stale-version, conflicting-evidence), a fixed corpus_hash, and a 64-character dataset_hash. Determinism means repeated loads produce identical hashes.

F0071.statement: load_dataset validates each file against the manifest SHA-256: appending even a single space to corpus.jsonl causes a 'SHA-256 mismatch' DatasetValidationError. File contents are therefore integrity-checked before use.

F0072.statement: load_dataset rejects malformed and semantically inconsistent records with specific messages: invalid JSON lines, non-object entries, blank lines, judgments referencing unknown queries or unknown targets, target-type mismatches, duplicate query IDs, queries without any judgment, and queries with only a zero-grade (no positive) judgment. These enforce referential and label-quality rules at load time.

F0073.statement: The dataset contract also validates manifest and record shape independently of files: DatasetManifest requires a minimum set of files (rejecting a truncated files list), CorpusRecord requires document_id for chunk records and forbids document_id on document records, and an unreadable/missing corpus.jsonl or invalid manifest produces DatasetValidationError. These are Pydantic validation errors surfaced at load time.

F0074.statement: score_ranking produces fixed retrieval metrics for a ranked list of result IDs against graded relevance judgments: recall@5/@10/@50, mrr@10, and nDCG@10. In the known-answer example ['negative','weak','best'] with grades {weak:1,best:3,negative:0}, all recalls are 1, mrr@10 is 0.5, and nDCG@10 follows the expected logarithmic formula, so the metric definitions are pinned and reproducible.

F0075.statement: score_ranking removes duplicate result IDs before applying cutoffs and keeps the full judged denominator for recall even when fewer results are returned: 60 copies of 'a' plus one 'b' against grades {a:3,b:2,c:1} yields recall@5 == recall@50 == 2/3 and mrr@10 == 1. Unjudged results and empty inputs produce zeros rather than errors, so metrics degrade gracefully.

F0076.statement: score_ranking rejects invalid judgments by raising ValueError when a grade is 0-only-invalid, negative, above 3, or a non-integer boolean, so grade validation is enforced at scoring time as well as at persistence time.

F0077.statement: corpus.prepare_corpus takes a dataset, settings, and an optional non-negative document_delay, enqueues durable ingestion jobs per corpus document, persists IngestionJob rows, and verifies prepared state. It reuses an already-succeeded durable job without re-running it or re-adding a document, and rejects a negative delay with a 'nonnegative' ValueError, making preparation idempotent and bounded.

F0078.statement: prepare_corpus treats persisted documents as immutable: when a stored document's content_hash differs from the expected hash it raises a 'differs' ValueError, and when a durable job returns RETRY_SCHEDULED the preparation aborts with a 'retry_scheduled' ValueError. This prevents silently searching an inconsistent corpus.

F0079.statement: corpus.verify_prepared requires a complete set of ingestion job receipts with matching index generations: missing jobs raise 'not prepared', a job missing its index checkpoint raises 'receipt', and stale generation IDs in the OpenSearch aggregation raise 'differs'. On success it returns 16 (the document count) and queries OpenSearch's documents aggregation for the scope's collection, meaning the indexed corpus must match the prepared scope before evaluation can proceed.

F0080.statement: Evaluation index setup is isolated and reusable: ensure_evaluation_index creates the index only when it does not already exist (a 404 creates, a subsequent 200 reuses without a second create), and the evaluation settings use a read alias prefixed 'hybrid-rag-eval-'. compact_corpus is invoked afterward, so the per-scope evaluation index is separate from production aliases and force-merged after preparation.

F0081.statement: Evaluation runs are deterministic given a fixed dataset and search function: calling evaluate twice with the same inputs produces identical per-query metrics (compare_reports(max_absolute_per_query_metric_delta) == 0), which supports regression comparison between runs.

F0082.statement: compare_reports rejects comparisons when report metadata differs in models or when query sets differ, raising ValueError with 'models' or 'query sets' messages.

F0083.statement: evaluate validates the dataset, raising ValueError mentioning 'unique' when judgments contain duplicate entries.

F0084.statement: save_report writes a JSON report (report.json) containing aggregate and per-query metrics keyed by mode, plus a markdown report (report.md) including a 'Per-query differences' section; per-query entries carry delta_vs_bm25 metrics relative to BM25.

F0085.statement: evaluation_scope is stable against dataset_hash changes but changes when corpus_hash or opensearch_index_schema_version change, and requires a document-type corpus (rejecting chunk-typed corpora with 'document corpora'), and selected_dataset rejects path-traversal style names like '../notes.txt'.

F0086.statement: benchmark_settings enforces a fixed evaluation budget (rerank_candidate_limit and rerank_result_limit both 100) independent of the base Settings value (which is 20).

F0087.statement: configuration() strips the rerank provider API key (cohere_api_key) from recorded configuration, so saved baseline metadata never contains credentials; run_baseline also records cache_state, rerank_fallback_count, code_revision/tracked_worktree_dirty from git, platform/processor, and adapter identifiers.

F0088.statement: evaluate paces queries with an explicit query_delay: it awaits asyncio.sleep(query_delay) between queries and rejects negative delays with a ValueError mentioning 'nonnegative'.

F0089.statement: EvaluationSearch.search supports the four modes in MODES, rejects unknown modes with 'Unknown search', rejects unsupported filters such as tenant_id with 'Unsupported', and rejects hits whose tenant/collection fall outside the evaluation scope with a ValueError mentioning 'outside'.

F0090.statement: EvaluationSearch applies tenant and collection scope in every OpenSearch request body, so retrieval is isolated per evaluation scope rather than relying only on client-side filtering.

F0091.statement: For each mode, search returns ranked document entries (document_id, chunk_id, rank) derived from retrieved chunks, with duplicate source chunk ids collapsed to a single document result.

F0092.statement: The debug search endpoint (/debug/search) validates dataset and scope selection (rejecting '../notes.txt' and caller-supplied tenant_ids with 422), returns results for each supported mode, and is disabled (404) when app_env is production.

F0093.statement: The debug endpoint maps preparation and retrieval failures to HTTP status codes: 409 when the corpus is not prepared, and 503 for RetrievalError/ProviderError unavailability.

F0094.statement: scifact.download_archive fetches the SciFact archive over HTTP, verifies its SHA-256 against a pinned constant, writes to a temporary '.partial' path, and removes the partial file on hash mismatch (raising 'SHA-256 mismatch').

F0095.statement: scifact.convert_archive converts the BEIR-style archive (corpus.jsonl, queries.jsonl, qrels/test.tsv) into the shared dataset contract deterministically: renamed document/query ids, sorted records, grades mapped onto the evaluation scale, and a version summary string; it rejects archives failing the pinned SHA-256 check.

F0096.statement: The scifact CLI exposes 'download' and 'validate' subcommands: download converts and reports corpus/query/judgment counts, validate reloads the dataset via load_dataset and prints dataset identity plus dataset_hash and writes a manifest.json recording the archive SHA-256.

F0097.statement: scifact.build_subset(source, output) deterministically builds an evaluation subset: running it twice on the same source and differing output paths yields datasets that compare equal (test_subset_is_repeatable_and_preserves_all_selected_judgments, test_selection_ignores_input_order_and_retains_complete_judgments).

F0098.statement: The subset produced contains exactly 500 corpus items and 30 queries, and its judgments equal the source dataset's judgments, with every judgment target_id contained in the corpus ids.

F0099.statement: Subset query selection is order-independent: selected queries are the 30 queries whose ids have the smallest sha256 of the string 'scifact-subset-v1:<query_id>', so the choice depends only on query ids, not input ordering.

F0100.statement: The subset build retains the complete set of judgments whose query_id belongs to the selected queries, and rejects/keeps nothing based on input order.

F0101.statement: build_subset enforces validation constraints: it raises ValueError mentioning 'at least 30' when the source dataset has fewer than 30 queries, and ValueError mentioning 'more than 500' when required documents exceed 500 (tests monkeypatch load_dataset to inject these conditions).

F0102.statement: The registered 'scifact-subset' dataset is reachable from the debug search API: selected_dataset(request.dataset) for that name returns a corpus of 500 documents (test_registered_subset_is_available_to_debug_api).

F0103.statement: A scifact CLI entry point ('scifact subset --source <path>') exists; scifact.main() reads sys.argv and writes the built subset to scifact.SUBSET_OUTPUT when no output is given, and the result is loadable via load_dataset.

F0104.statement: The subset's manifest records source license 'CC BY-NC 2.0', indicating license provenance is preserved in the built dataset manifest.

F0105.statement: The evaluation dataset corpus contract (corpus.schema.json) requires id, type, and text per record; type is one of 'document' or 'chunk'; optional fields include document_id, title, and metadata; extra properties are forbidden.

F0106.statement: The evaluation judgment contract (judgment.schema.json) requires query_id, target_type, target_id, and relevance_grade, with relevance_grade an integer from 0 to 3 and target_type one of 'document' or 'chunk'.

F0107.statement: The evaluation query contract (query.schema.json) requires id and text; optional fields include category, expected_answer, key_facts (array of strings), and metadata_filters (object), suggesting supported filtering and answer/key-fact metadata.

F0108.statement: The dataset manifest contract (manifest.schema.json) enforces schema_version 'evaluation-dataset-v1', purpose 'evaluation', a source object (with optional url, 64-hex archive_sha256, and license), and exactly three files enumerated as corpus.jsonl, queries.jsonl, judgments.jsonl each with a 64-hex sha256 — so dataset integrity is pinned by per-file hashes.

F0109.statement: Dataset manifests require a non-empty name, version, and description and a source.name, indicating versioned, described datasets with named provenance.

F0110.statement: Entity ids across corpus, query, and judgment schemas follow the same pattern '^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$', indicating a shared identifier convention across evaluation records.

F0111.statement: load_dataset is reused both by the subset builder (to read source datasets) and by consumers (tests call load_dataset on built output), making it the read/validation boundary the builder depends on.

F0112.statement: The schemas declare an https://hybrid-rag-search.local host and fixed file set (corpus.jsonl, queries.jsonl, judgments.jsonl), implying evaluation datasets are stored as a three-file JSONL bundle plus a manifest; this file layout is inferred from schema constraints, not observed runtime code.
